newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul banking shares seen weakening on ratings.
newsitem.headline: Seoul banking shares seen weakening on ratings.

text.p: Bank shares were expected to be hit by an announcement Standard & Poor's Corp might cut the ratings of five Korean banks, brokers said on Thursday.
They said Ssangyong Group shares would rebound from their limit-lows, but remain weak as investors were still concerned about rumours of cash flow problems.

"The market in general is expected to escape from the initial shock by Kia, Jinro and Ssangyong woes," said Jo Jae-hoon at Daewoo Securities. "But unstable won/dollar and rising interest rates have cast a gloom on the market.
The stock index gained 4.60 points to 730.58 on Wednesday.

S&P said in a statement that its ratingaction reflected the deteriorating asset quality and heightening industry risks faced by Korean banks as defaults continue to emerge among Korea's industrial conglomerates.
Albert Jan Hofman, head of Asian fixed-income research at ABN Amro Hoare Govett in Hong Kong, said "Korea First Bank is definitely affected most."
Brokers said margin loans exceeding customers deposit also pressured investor sentiment.
